_help: Paralegal persona: gate for submit_memo_to_partner. Every threshold has a one-sentence why.
on_ezio_failure_why: We fail closed: without Ezio, non-citation claims (e.g. what an Amendment says) are unchecked, so a human reviews; our citation check still runs and BLOCKs fabricated or misstated cases even while Ezio is down.
tier_decisions_why: GREEN is never sufficient on its own (citation checks can still block); YELLOW/RED say something is off but the tier alone doesn't say what, so a human looks; hard BLOCKs come only from specific evidence (fabricated case, misstated cite, contradicted claim).
when_claim_contradicted_why: Rule 6: a claim Ezio's fact-check contradicts is a concrete, sourced error, and a partner relying on it is the exact harm we gate.

tone.why: Below 60 matches Ezio's own RED cutoff for a single dimension; memos must be neutral (rule 4), and a GREEN overall tier can hide one bad dimension.

bias.why: A one-sided memo misleads the partner about litigation risk; 60 is the same RED cutoff, so ordinary analytical framing passes.

agreement.why: Low agreement means the draft echoes rather than analyzes; below the RED cutoff a human should confirm it isn't sycophantic.

when_accuracy_not_scored_why: Rule 5: 'not scored' just means Ezio found no public claims; our citation lists are the accuracy check for case law, and a memo with no citations is fine to submit.
when_accuracy_unavailable_why: If the fact-check is down, a constitutional or statutory claim could be wrong with nobody checking it, so we hold rather than approve blind; fabricated citations are still blocked outright.
